title: Middlemen exploitation strips farmers of fair market prices
description: Smallholder farmers, most of whom own less than 0.1 hectares of land, are largely disconnected from formal markets and sell produce to middlemen at low prices. These intermediaries resell at much higher margins in urban markets, widening the price spread between producer and consumer and leaving farmers little income to reinvest.
severity_or_scale: 57.5% of agricultural households own under 0.1 hectares of land

title: Post-harvest losses destroy a third of fruit and vegetable output
description: Poor storage, transport, and processing facilities cause massive spoilage between farm and market. Wholesalers in open-air markets routinely dump produce that rots within days, with some days seeing up to half of received consignments discarded.
severity_or_scale: Post-harvest losses estimated at 20-50% of fresh produce, 30-40% for fruits and vegetables specifically

title: Near-total absence of cold storage and cold-chain infrastructure
description: Cold storage that could cut spoilage by more than 75% exists only in fragmented, mostly private form concentrated around Kathmandu, and is inaccessible to most farmers, especially in remote hill districts. Farmers there have no way to preserve perishable produce even a week beyond harvest.
severity_or_scale: Cold storage could reduce wastage by over 75%, but coverage remains minimal nationwide

title: Chronic fertilizer shortages fuel black-market price gouging
description: Government-subsidized urea, DAP and potash fertilizers imported through state companies meet only about half of national demand, and supply breakdowns mean farmers often cannot get fertilizer at planting time. Smuggled fertilizer then sells at inflated prices to farmers desperate to save their season's crop.
severity_or_scale: Annual fertilizer imports of 350,000-450,000 tonnes cover about 50% of estimated demand of 700,000 tonnes

title: Erratic monsoons and winter drought undermine rain-fed farming
description: Most Nepali farmers, particularly in the mid-hills, depend on rainfall rather than irrigation infrastructure. Recent winter droughts and delayed monsoons have cut rice yields by up to 20% in some Terai districts, with the 2025 monsoon drought contributing to an estimated 10% national drop in rice production.
severity_or_scale: Rice yields down up to 20% in affected districts; ~10% national rice production decline in 2025

title: Land fragmentation blocks commercial-scale farming
description: Generational subdivision of family land has left most Nepali farms too small and scattered to mechanize or farm at commercial scale. This structural fragmentation keeps a large share of agriculture at subsistence level and discourages investment in modern equipment.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified precisely, but the majority of holdings are under 1 hectare

title: Growing reliance on imported seeds creates supply vulnerability
description: Nepali farmers increasingly depend on seeds imported from India rather than locally adapted or saved varieties, a shift that raises costs and exposed farmers to severe shortages during disruptions like COVID-19 border closures. Domestic seed-multiplication and certification systems remain underdeveloped.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Milk production deficit forces costly dairy imports
description: Domestic milk production meets only around 80% of national consumption needs, with demand growing twice as fast as supply. Urban centers rely on dairy imports from India worth billions of rupees annually, while only a small fraction of Nepali dairy farmers are commercially organized.
severity_or_scale: Domestic production ~72 litres/person/year vs ~92 litres/person/year required; annual dairy imports around NPR 2 billion

title: Recurring avian flu outbreaks devastate poultry farmers
description: H5N1 bird flu outbreaks have repeatedly torn through Nepal's commercial and backyard poultry farms, forcing mass culling of birds and destruction of eggs and feed. Small farmers absorb losses that government compensation only partially covers, while consumers face price spikes.
severity_or_scale: A single 2026 outbreak wave led to culling of 479,000+ birds and 694,000+ eggs across 10 districts; poultry industry valued around Rs 60 billion

title: Large cardamom export earnings overly dependent on one market
description: Nepal is the world's largest producer of large cardamom, a high-value spice export, but roughly 99% of exports go to a single buyer, India, leaving farmers and traders exposed to price swings and trade-policy shifts with no diversification cushion.
severity_or_scale: India absorbs ~99% of Nepal's large cardamom exports; Nepal produces ~68% of global output

title: Low mechanization keeps farm productivity and incomes depressed
description: Manual labor still dominates Nepali agriculture, with limited access to tractors, threshers, and other equipment, particularly in the hills where terrain and fragmented plots make mechanization economically unviable for individual farmers.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified
source: general knowledge / ScienceDirect agriculture modernization review

title: Weak agricultural extension services leave farmers without technical advice
description: Government agricultural extension offices are understaffed, so farmers often lack timely, practical advice on pest management, crop selection, or new techniques. This gap is especially acute in remote hill and mountain districts far from district agriculture offices.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified
source: general knowledge / Nepal Economic Forum agriculture sector analyses

title: Collateral requirements shut smallholders and women out of agricultural credit
description: Formal agricultural loans typically require land as collateral, excluding tenant farmers and many women who do not hold land titles. While some collateral-free schemes have emerged, most farmers still rely on informal, high-interest moneylenders for working capital.
severity_or_scale: Women entrepreneurs face an estimated $321 million financing gap

title: Unregulated pesticide use puts consumers at risk
description: Farmers increasingly overuse chemical pesticides to boost yields and shelf-appeal, especially for vegetables sold into Kathmandu markets, with testing repeatedly finding residues far above safe thresholds. Weak inspection and lab capacity mean contaminated produce regularly reaches consumers.
severity_or_scale: Lab testing found pesticide residue levels of 45-65% (unsafe threshold) in samples of chilli, pumpkin, and gourd from several districts

title: Contract farming agreements offer smallholders little real protection
description: Contract farming has been promoted as a way to guarantee smallholders stable buyers and prices, but weak legal enforcement means contracts are frequently broken by either party, undermining trust and limiting the model's adoption as a market-access solution.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Inadequate rural veterinary services let livestock disease spread unchecked
description: Smallholder livestock farmers, who make up the vast majority of the dairy and meat sector, have little access to veterinary care, vaccination, or breeding support, making outbreaks harder to contain and limiting productivity gains.
severity_or_scale: Only 14-16% of livestock farmers are commercialized
source: general knowledge / dairy value chain research

title: Expensive large-scale irrigation systems fail smallholders
description: Costly government-built irrigation schemes, such as the Rani Jamara system in Kailali, are often designed for large contiguous fields and fail to reliably deliver water to fragmented smallholder plots when needed, while cheaper decentralized solutions remain unevenly available.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Aging farming workforce as youth migrate away from agriculture
description: With young Nepalis increasingly leaving villages for foreign labor migration or urban jobs, farming is left disproportionately to older family members and women, straining household labor capacity during planting and harvest and accelerating land abandonment in hill districts.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Severe shortage and urban concentration of doctors
description: Nepal has only about 0.17 doctors per 1,000 population, and roughly 60% of practicing doctors are based in urban areas even though the large majority of the population lives rurally. This maldistribution leaves entire districts with minimal physician coverage for serious illness or emergencies.
severity_or_scale: 0.17 doctors per 1,000 population; 60% of doctors in urban areas; 81% of population is rural

title: Brain drain of doctors abroad depletes the health workforce
description: More than 500 Nepali doctors emigrate each year for better pay and working conditions abroad, undercutting years of investment in medical training and worsening the shortage of specialists available domestically, particularly outside Kathmandu.
severity_or_scale: 500+ doctors emigrate annually

title: Public hospitals face chronic essential medicine shortages
description: Procurement bottlenecks, budget delays, and weak supply-chain management mean public health facilities frequently run out of essential medicines, forcing pharmacists into workarounds like emergency purchases or borrowing from other hospitals, and patients into paying out of pocket.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified precisely

title: Life-saving chemotherapy drugs face nationwide shortages
description: An acute, nationwide shortage of platinum-based chemotherapy drugs has disrupted cancer treatment across Nepal, with government price controls contributing to reduced supply and patients' families resorting to black-market purchases to continue treatment.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified precisely (nationwide disruption reported in 2026)

title: Counterfeit and substandard medicines circulate widely
description: Weak regulatory enforcement and porous cross-border drug supply chains, especially from India, allow substandard or fake medicines into the Nepali market, endangering patients on long-term medication whose potency and safety cannot be reliably verified at point of sale.
severity_or_scale: Nepal imports about 70% of its medicine demand, heightening exposure to counterfeit supply

title: Mental health treatment gap leaves most sufferers untreated
description: Among Nepalis who screen positive for depression or alcohol use disorder, only a small fraction receive any treatment within a year, and fewer still access it through primary healthcare. Barriers include inability to afford care, severe stigma, and scarcity of trained mental health professionals outside Kathmandu.
severity_or_scale: Only 8.1% of people with depression and 5.1% with alcohol use disorder received treatment in a 12-month period

title: Suicide rates have surged amid inadequate mental health care
description: Unemployment, financial stress, migration-related family separation, and social stigma are cited as drivers behind a sharp rise in suicide in Nepal, compounding a mental healthcare system that lacks capacity, funding, and public literacy to intervene early.
severity_or_scale: Suicide rates reported to have risen roughly 72% over the past decade

title: Long travel times required to reach any health facility
description: In much of rural and mountainous Nepal, reaching even a basic health post requires hours of travel, particularly during the monsoon when roads become impassable. This delays treatment for emergencies like childbirth complications and discourages routine preventive care.
severity_or_scale: One 2021 estimate found ~95% of the population needs 60 minutes of walking to reach a health facility

title: Telemedicine remains constrained by connectivity and electrification gaps
description: Platforms offering remote consultation and e-prescriptions show promise for reaching underserved mountain communities, but scaling them is limited by unreliable electricity and internet in the very areas that need them most, plus a lack of trained local health workers.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: High out-of-pocket spending pushes families into debt over healthcare
description: With health insurance coverage limited and public facilities often under-supplied, Nepali households frequently pay directly for medicines, diagnostics, and private treatment, a burden that during the recent cooperative financial crisis has reportedly caused some families to skip medical care altogether.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified precisely
source: general knowledge / Nepal health financing literature

title: Diagnostic and laboratory infrastructure concentrated in cities
description: Advanced diagnostic services such as imaging, pathology, and specialized lab testing are heavily concentrated in Kathmandu, Pokhara, and a handful of other cities, forcing rural patients to travel long distances or go undiagnosed for treatable conditions.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Weak drug regulatory capacity struggles to keep pace with imports
description: Nepal's drug regulatory authority has limited staffing and testing capacity relative to the volume of pharmaceutical imports and local production it must oversee, making consistent quality assurance across thousands of registered and unregistered products difficult.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Rural health posts often lack staffing beyond a single provider
description: Many rural health posts are staffed by a single auxiliary health worker or nurse rather than a doctor, meaning residents needing anything beyond basic first aid must travel to a district hospital, often a multi-hour journey away.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Maternal and newborn care access gaps in remote districts
description: Women in remote hill and mountain districts often lack timely access to skilled birth attendants and emergency obstetric care, increasing risks during complicated deliveries; telemedicine and mobile health pilots attempt to close this gap but remain limited in scale.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Health worker density falls far short of WHO thresholds
description: Nepal has around 0.67 doctors and nurses per 1,000 population, well below the World Health Organization's benchmark for adequate coverage, meaning the country is structurally short of the clinical staff needed to deliver basic universal health coverage.
severity_or_scale: 0.67 skilled health workers per 1,000 population vs WHO SDG threshold of 4.45

title: Stigma among healthcare providers themselves blocks mental health care-seeking
description: Beyond public stigma, many healthcare workers in Nepal hold stigmatizing attitudes toward mental illness, which discourages patients from disclosing symptoms and results in under-diagnosis and under-referral even when patients do reach a clinic.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Teacher absenteeism plagues rural and remote schools
description: Studies describe teacher absenteeism in remote hill schools running as high as 20-40%, with some teachers effectively becoming ghost teachers who appear only occasionally to record attendance while drawing a full salary. Weak local oversight and reluctance of urban-trained teachers to accept remote postings drive the problem.
severity_or_scale: Absenteeism estimated at 15-40% nationally, 20-35% in remote hill districts

title: Widening quality gap between rural and urban schools
description: Public schools in rural areas lag far behind private and urban schools in facilities and qualified teacher ratios, with rural dropout rates running significantly higher than urban ones as students fall behind, especially in subjects needed for national exams.
severity_or_scale: Rural dropout rates reported ~30% higher than urban areas

title: Acute shortage of subject teachers in math, science, and English
description: Rural schools in districts like Gulmi report it has become nearly impossible to find qualified math, science, and English teachers, since most licensed subject-specialist graduates prefer urban postings, causing a measurable decline in subject-specific learning outcomes.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified precisely

title: Mass exodus of students abroad drains higher education
description: A record number of Nepali students obtain No Objection Certificates to study overseas rather than pursue higher education domestically, leaving many colleges struggling to fill seats and some facing closure, driven by perceived lack of opportunity and political instability at home.
severity_or_scale: 115,000+ NOCs issued in 2025 alone, up from 44,800 a few years earlier; ~600 applications processed daily

title: Vocational training curricula are decades out of date
description: Much of Nepal's technical and vocational education (CTEVT) content was designed years or decades ago and has not kept pace with industry needs — for example, hospitality graduates reportedly do not know how to use modern property-management software used by hotels today.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: High youth unemployment despite rising education levels
description: Nepal's young unemployment rate significantly exceeds the world average, reflecting a mismatch between what schools and colleges teach and what employers need, alongside a limited domestic job market that pushes graduates toward foreign labor migration instead.
severity_or_scale: Youth unemployment rate of 20.8% in 2024

title: Colleges face existential enrollment collapse
description: As students opt to study abroad rather than domestically, many private and community colleges across Nepal report enrollment shortfalls in the thousands, pushing some toward closure and threatening the broader post-secondary education ecosystem.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified precisely (described as 'thousands' short at many colleges)

title: Public school facilities lag far behind private schools
description: Community (public) schools generally have poorer infrastructure — classrooms, labs, sanitation — compared to private schools, reinforcing a two-tier education system where wealthier families opt out of the public system, further starving it of advocacy and mixed-income enrollment.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Federal decentralization created confusion in education governance
description: The shift of education administration to local governments under federalism has produced inconsistent implementation capacity across Nepal's hundreds of municipalities, with some units lacking the technical staff to manage teacher recruitment, curriculum, or budget effectively.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Foundational learning gaps compound as students progress
description: Students who fall behind in foundational subjects like math in early secondary grades often have no mechanism to catch up, meaning gaps compound by the national SEE exam, disproportionately affecting rural and lower-income students who lack access to private tutoring.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Child labor keeps children out of school
description: An estimated 1.1 million children in Nepal are engaged in child labor, mostly in agriculture and domestic work, which directly competes with school attendance and perpetuates a cycle of poverty and low educational attainment across generations.
severity_or_scale: 1.1 million children in child labor

title: Weak university research capacity limits innovation pipeline
description: Nepali universities generally lack funding, lab infrastructure, and incentive structures for research output, meaning few of the applied research findings needed to inform sectors like agriculture, health, or engineering are generated domestically.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Limited digital learning infrastructure outside urban centers
description: Remote and online learning tools require reliable electricity, devices, and internet that many rural schools and students still lack, meaning the shift toward digital education has widened rather than narrowed rural-urban gaps.
severity_or_scale: National digital literacy estimated at only around 31%

title: Female teacher shortage in remote districts affects girls' retention
description: A lack of female teachers and gender-sensitive facilities like separate toilets in many rural schools contributes to higher dropout rates for adolescent girls, particularly after puberty, compounding existing gender gaps in secondary completion.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Political interference in teacher hiring and transfers enables patronage
description: Political interference in teacher recruitment, transfer, and promotion decisions is widely reported, allowing well-connected teachers to secure comfortable urban postings while less-connected teachers are sent to remote schools regardless of subject-matter fit.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Nepal's economy is dangerously dependent on remittances
description: Remittances sent home by millions of migrant workers make up roughly a quarter of Nepal's GDP, propping up household consumption and the balance of payments but leaving the economy highly exposed to shocks in destination-country labor markets or migration policy.
severity_or_scale: Remittances ~26.6% of GDP in 2023; inflows of ~Rs 1,723 billion (~$12.6B) in FY2024/25

title: Remittance transfer costs remain a persistent tax on migrant families
description: Sending money home from abroad costs Nepali migrants an average of around 4.5% of the amount transferred through formal channels, a meaningful drag on household income for families that depend heavily on these flows for daily expenses.
severity_or_scale: Average remittance transfer cost ~4.5%

title: Informal hundi channels bypass the formal banking system
description: A substantial share of remittances flows through hundi, an informal value-transfer network that lets migrants avoid formal transfer fees and taxes, but leaves flows untracked, undermines formal financial-sector development, and offers senders no consumer protection if funds go missing.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified precisely ('substantial share' of remittances via informal channels)

title: Most remittance-receiving households remain unbanked
description: Despite the scale of remittance inflows, a large majority of receiving households, especially in rural areas, lack formal bank accounts, forcing reliance on cash pickup agents and limiting their ability to save, invest, or build credit history.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified precisely ('large majority' of rural remittance-receiving households unbanked)

title: Remittance inflows have made Nepali exports less competitive
description: The steady inflow of remittance dollars has appreciated Nepal's real effective exchange rate substantially since 2000, a classic Dutch disease effect that, combined with rising domestic costs, has made non-remittance productive sectors like manufacturing and agriculture less competitive internationally.
severity_or_scale: ~16% real effective exchange rate appreciation since 2000 attributed to remittances

title: Digital payment adoption among small merchants remains very low
description: Even though most formal micro, small, and medium enterprises have broadband access, fewer than one in ten used electronic payments as of 2023, reflecting low digital and financial literacy and limited merchant-side infrastructure for card or QR payments outside major cities.
severity_or_scale: ~90% of formal MSMEs have broadband access but <10% used electronic payments in 2023

title: Fragmented digital payment platforms lack interoperability
description: Nepal's growing roster of mobile wallets and digital banking apps often cannot transact seamlessly with each other, forcing consumers and merchants to maintain multiple accounts and undermining the convenience that should drive broader digital payment adoption.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Cooperative savings scandal wiped out billions in household deposits
description: Operators of savings and credit cooperatives embezzled depositor funds, targeting retirees, laborers, vendors, and farmers lured by high promised interest rates, diverting money into real estate speculation and personal ventures. The fallout triggered panic withdrawals, closures, and a rural credit crunch, with some families reportedly skipping medical care as a result.
severity_or_scale: At least Rs 87.89 billion (~$630M) in documented embezzlement across dozens of institutions; ~94,000 sector jobs affected

title: Women entrepreneurs face a large, persistent financing gap
description: Women-owned businesses in Nepal struggle to access formal credit because loans typically require land collateral that many women do not hold in their own name. Despite subsidized women-entrepreneurship loan interest rates, the structural collateral barrier keeps a substantial financing gap in place.
severity_or_scale: Estimated $321 million financing gap for women entrepreneurs

title: High collateral requirements and interest rates choke SME lending
description: Small and medium enterprises across sectors report collateral requirements averaging around 130% of loan value, alongside high interest rates and complex application procedures, pushing many toward informal lenders or personal savings instead of formal bank credit.
severity_or_scale: Collateral requirements averaging ~130% of loan value

title: Rising digital fraud and phishing threaten consumer trust in fintech
description: As mobile banking and digital wallets expand, so do reports of fraud, phishing, and data breaches targeting users unfamiliar with digital security practices, and Nepal still lacks a widely trusted framework to protect consumers and rapidly resolve disputes.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified
source: general knowledge / Nepal digital payments coverage

title: Nascent venture capital ecosystem starves startups of growth capital
description: Nepal's venture capital industry is thin and concentrated in a handful of sectors, and government startup funding schemes announced with fanfare produced little to no actual disbursement, leaving most entrepreneurs to bootstrap or rely on scarce angel investment.
severity_or_scale: Nepal's total startup capital raised over a decade doesn't approach India's $10B raised in 2023 alone

title: Complex rules deter foreign capital and payment gateway access
description: Entrepreneurs report that bringing foreign investment into a Nepali startup involves complex regulatory procedures, and that accessing mainstream international payment gateways remains difficult, limiting the growth of Nepal's digital and export-oriented businesses.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Rural and marginalized-caste populations lag furthest behind in digital finance
description: Internet access and digital payment adoption vary significantly by geography, caste, and gender, meaning fintech expansion concentrated in Kathmandu and among educated urban men leaves rural women and marginalized groups least equipped to benefit from digital financial tools.
severity_or_scale: 37% of higher-caste households have internet access vs 21% of Dalit households

title: Domestic remittance and account restrictions have triggered new financial exclusion
description: Recent regulatory changes around domestic money transfer and account closures have cut off people without adequate access to digital payment tools or bank accounts from moving money within Nepal, disproportionately affecting low-income and informal-sector workers.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Extreme seasonality leaves tourism workers without income for months
description: Nepal's trekking and mountaineering seasons are concentrated in narrow spring and autumn windows, meaning tens of thousands of guides, porters, and lodge staff face months of no income in the off-season, with no unemployment insurance or income smoothing mechanism.
severity_or_scale: Seasonal support-labor employment estimated at 40,000-50,000 people

title: Porters work without contracts, insurance, or guaranteed pay
description: Freelance porters, who carry heavy loads for trekkers at lower pay than guides, are often the least protected workers in the tourism value chain, lacking written contracts or insurance, so a canceled trek can mean zero income that week with no recourse.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Inadequate tourist safety and rescue infrastructure
description: Trekkers and climbers in remote areas often cannot count on timely rescue services or emergency medical care, and government investment in safety infrastructure along popular routes has lagged the growth in visitor numbers.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Domestic aviation has a troubled safety record
description: Nepal's mountainous terrain, unpredictable weather, and inconsistent implementation of safety recommendations from past crash investigations have contributed to a high rate of aviation accidents on domestic routes serving trekking and remote-area tourism, undermining traveler confidence.
severity_or_scale: 112 aviation accidents since 1956 claiming 965 lives; 4 accidents and 21 serious incidents in 2023 alone

title: High OTA commissions squeeze small hotels and homestays
description: Online travel agencies like Booking.com and Agoda typically charge commissions of 15-25% on bookings, a steep cost for Nepal's thousands of small, often family-run homestays and guesthouses that nonetheless depend on these platforms for visibility to foreign tourists.
severity_or_scale: OTA commissions of 15-25%; ~6,500 registered homestays across 1,500 villages

title: Small accommodation providers struggle to accept foreign card payments
description: Many small Nepali hotels and homestays cannot easily accept international credit cards due to high merchant fees and limited banking infrastructure, pushing many toward cash-only transactions less convenient for foreign tourists used to card payments.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Everest region overwhelmed by waste and overcrowding
description: Surging visitor numbers to the Everest region have outpaced waste management capacity, with an estimated 200 tons of trash left on the mountain and surrounding trails annually and inadequate sanitation infrastructure for the volume of trekkers.
severity_or_scale: Everest region visitors grew from ~3,600 in 1979 to over 58,000 in 2019; ~200 tons of trash left annually

title: Road and vehicle safety failures cause frequent tourist accidents
description: Poor-quality road infrastructure, aging vehicle fleets, and inconsistent driver training and licensing contribute to transportation-related accidents affecting tourists traveling between trekking trailheads and tourist destinations.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Homestay and small hospitality operators lack digital marketing skills
description: Many rural homestay and lodge operators lack the digital literacy and tools to manage online listings, respond to international inquiries, or run basic digital marketing, leaving them dependent on intermediaries even as most bookings now originate online.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Tourism product remains overly concentrated in trekking and mountaineering
description: Nepal's tourism economy is heavily weighted toward trekking and mountaineering circuits, with comparatively underdeveloped cultural, wellness, or business-tourism offerings, limiting the sector's ability to spread economic benefit more evenly across regions and seasons.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Slow recovery for tourism workers after external shocks
description: Events like the COVID-19 pandemic and periodic natural disasters have repeatedly devastated the incomes of guides, porters, and hospitality staff, and formal social protection or rapid-recovery support for this predominantly informal workforce remains limited.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Mandatory guide policy compliance creates friction for trekkers and operators
description: A newly enforced requirement for independent trekkers to hire licensed guides on many routes has created adjustment friction for both budget travelers and smaller trekking agencies who must rapidly scale up guide availability and pricing structures to comply.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Limited entertainment infrastructure shortens visitor stays
description: A shortage of developed evening entertainment, cultural programming, and visitor amenities beyond trekking itself is cited as a reason foreign tourists spend fewer days and less money per visit than in competing destinations.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Trekking permit paperwork remains fragmented and cumbersome
description: Multiple permits issued by different offices create a fragmented, sometimes confusing process for independent trekkers and smaller operators trying to book trips from abroad, compared to more streamlined single-window systems elsewhere.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Foreign booking friction from limited international marketing reach
description: Beyond well-known routes like Everest and Annapurna, many of Nepal's tourism products such as lesser-known treks and homestays have limited visibility on the international platforms foreign travelers use to plan trips, restricting demand generation outside a handful of famous itineraries.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Nearly 40% of rural households live far from any road
description: Roughly 40% of rural households live two or more hours from a road, and even where roads exist, many are unpaved gravel or dirt tracks that become dangerous or impassable in bad weather, cutting communities off from markets, schools, and health services.
severity_or_scale: ~40% of rural households live 2+ hours from a road; only ~42% of roads nationally are blacktopped

title: Seasonal impassability strands rural communities during monsoon
description: Earthen and gravel roads, which make up well over half the rural road network, are frequently unusable during the rainy season, meaning entire communities can be effectively cut off from vehicle access for months, disrupting supply of goods and emergency transport.
severity_or_scale: 34.25% of roads are earthen/fair-weather; 23.55% graveled

title: New road construction is worsening landslide risk
description: Poorly engineered roads cut into fragile mountain geology are destabilizing slopes and increasing landslide frequency, with research linking rapid expansion of earthen roads between 2016-2018 to a significant rise in landslide-affected areas.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified precisely (described as a 'significant increase' in landslide-affected area)

title: Poor road maintenance erodes value of past infrastructure investment
description: Even paved roads frequently fall into disrepair due to inadequate ongoing maintenance funding and coordination, so gains from road-building are steadily lost, requiring repeated costly reconstruction rather than lower-cost preventive upkeep.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Last-mile e-commerce delivery is unreliable outside Kathmandu Valley
description: Warehousing and logistics networks are concentrated around Kathmandu, Birgunj, and Pokhara, and mountainous terrain plus poor rural roads make last-mile delivery to smaller towns and villages slow, expensive, or simply unavailable.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Nepal's fuel supply depends entirely on a single land route and supplier
description: As a landlocked country, Nepal sources virtually all petroleum products through the Indian Oil Corporation via a single land route, a dependency that leaves the country acutely vulnerable to supply disruptions or diplomatic tensions with India.
severity_or_scale: Fuel imports valued at up to Rs 1 billion/day during peak periods

title: Recurrent Nepal-India border friction disrupts cross-border trade
description: Periodic customs crackdowns or political disputes at the Nepal-India border have repeatedly caused long truck queues, stranded containers, and shortages of imported essentials like cooking gas and medicine, given how much of Nepal's trade flows through a handful of border crossings.
severity_or_scale: A 2026 customs crackdown left thousands of containers stranded at border points

title: Landlocked status forces reliance on Indian ports for global trade
description: With no direct sea access, Nepal's international trade beyond India and China depends on transiting through Indian ports, mainly Kolkata, adding cost, time, and diplomatic dependency to every shipment destined for or coming from third countries.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Underdeveloped rail and multimodal transport increases logistics costs
description: Nepal has minimal domestic rail infrastructure and limited multimodal integration, meaning nearly all freight movement relies on trucks over difficult mountain roads, raising per-unit transport costs compared to countries with more diversified freight networks.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Kathmandu Valley traffic congestion wastes time and worsens pollution
description: Rapid growth in private vehicle ownership combined with limited public transit and poor traffic management has made Kathmandu Valley's roads increasingly congested, with residents losing significant time annually to delays that also compound the valley's air pollution problem.
severity_or_scale: Residents reportedly spend ~120 hours per year in traffic congestion

title: High transport costs inflate consumer prices in remote districts
description: The combination of poor roads, long distances, and limited competition among transporters means the cost of moving goods to remote hill and mountain districts is passed on to consumers, who pay significantly more for basic goods than urban residents.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Limited formal transport companies serving remote regions
description: Beyond a handful of national courier and freight companies, remote regions are served mostly by informal transporters and local bus/jeep operators without standardized service levels or tracking, making reliable business logistics difficult to plan outside major urban corridors.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: History of crippling load-shedding disrupted daily life and business
description: Before major hydropower capacity came online around 2017-2018, Nepal endured years of severe power cuts of up to 18 hours a day, devastating small businesses and household life and pushing many to rely on costly diesel generators or inverters.
severity_or_scale: Power cuts of up to 18 hours/day at the peak of the crisis

title: Transmission bottlenecks now force wasted hydropower during monsoon surplus
description: Having gone from chronic shortage to seasonal surplus, Nepal now faces the opposite problem: inadequate transmission and export infrastructure means large amounts of hydropower generated during high-flow monsoon months cannot be used domestically or exported, forcing regulators to order curtailment.
severity_or_scale: An estimated 1,000+ MW of generated electricity currently wasted due to grid/export limits; 1,665 GWh wasted in 2023

title: Cross-border export capacity to India and Bangladesh remains capped
description: Nepal's ability to monetize surplus hydropower by exporting to India and Bangladesh is limited by shared transmission infrastructure capacity, with India at times blocking additional export allocations, leaving Nepali hydropower developers unable to sell power they can generate.
severity_or_scale: India-Bangladesh cross-border line capacity capped at 1,000 MW, constraining additional Nepal exports

title: Firewood remains the dominant cooking fuel despite grid expansion
description: Roughly 84% of Nepali households still rely primarily on firewood for cooking, rising to 95% in mountain regions, driving deforestation, indoor air pollution-related illness, and time burdens (mostly on women) spent collecting fuel.
severity_or_scale: 84% of households primarily use firewood; 95% in mountain regions

title: Nepal Oil Corporation's chronic losses threaten fuel supply stability
description: The state fuel monopoly has repeatedly reported selling petroleum products below cost, accumulating heavy periodic losses and struggling to pay its sole supplier on time, a dynamic that has triggered supply cuts and shortages when dues went unpaid.
severity_or_scale: Reported losses of around $52.78 million per fortnight in past crisis periods

title: Rural electrification gains coexist with reliability gaps
description: Micro-hydropower has extended basic electricity access to tens of thousands of rural households not reached by the national grid, but many of these systems face maintenance, capacity, and seasonal water-flow challenges that leave supply less reliable than grid connections in cities.
severity_or_scale: 11,300+ registered micro-hydropower plants benefiting almost 35,000 rural households as of 2024

title: Fuel and LPG shortages recur during India border disruptions
description: Because Nepal maintains only limited domestic petroleum and LPG reserves and imports depend entirely on the single land route from India, any border disruption rapidly threatens household cooking-gas supply, as industry associations have repeatedly warned.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified precisely

title: Seasonal hydropower generation mismatch causes dry-season shortages
description: Because most of Nepal's hydropower is run-of-river rather than reservoir-based, generation drops sharply in dry winter months just as demand often rises, creating a structural mismatch that can still require imports or rationing despite monsoon-season surplus capacity.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Industrial users face unreliable power quality affecting production
description: Voltage fluctuations and localized outages continue to affect manufacturing and industrial users even after the end of nationwide load-shedding, creating equipment damage risk and productivity losses for factories that cannot fully rely on uninterrupted grid quality.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Bureaucratic delays slow hydropower project licensing and financing
description: Hydropower developers describe lengthy, multi-agency licensing, land acquisition, and environmental approval processes that delay projects for years, adding financing costs and discouraging domestic and foreign private investment in a sector with huge natural potential.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Developers bear financial risk when transmission isn't ready on time
description: Hydropower project developers report that when their plants are generation-ready but the associated transmission line is not, they still must service bank loan interest with no revenue, and existing compensation mechanisms for such delays are considered inadequate.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Petroleum remains Nepal's largest, least diversified import category
description: Fuel imports are Nepal's single largest import expense and a major driver of trade deficit and tax revenue, yet supplier diversification such as a 2015 framework agreement with China has seen little practical progress, leaving energy security tied to one relationship.
severity_or_scale: Fuel described as Nepal's largest import and biggest contributor to tax revenue

title: Incomplete and inconsistent land-record digitization invites fraud
description: While land records have been digitized across most survey and revenue offices, the effort has proceeded with little systematic research into what safeguards prevent manipulation, and paper records remain vulnerable to tampering or destruction where digitization is incomplete.
severity_or_scale: Digitization completed in land offices nationwide except a couple of districts where conflict-era records were destroyed

title: Dual land ownership disputes rooted in conflict-era record gaps
description: Absent claimants, unpaid dues, and unidentified owners, often stemming from disruption of record-keeping during the Maoist insurgency, have produced widespread dual-ownership disputes that reduce agricultural productivity and tie up land in litigation for years.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Landless settler (sukumbasi) crisis defies repeated government promises
description: Hundreds of thousands of landless and informally settled families live in legal limbo, facing periodic eviction threats without adequate resettlement, as successive governments have promised land redistribution or formalization programs that have repeatedly stalled.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified precisely (described as a long-running national crisis)

title: Haphazard urban expansion outpaces planning capacity
description: Kathmandu Valley's urban growth has occurred largely without risk-sensitive planning, producing unplanned settlement patterns, overcrowding, and construction that ignores hazard zones, a pattern researchers link directly to Nepal's high vulnerability to earthquake and flood disasters.
severity_or_scale: Built-up area in Kathmandu Valley grew 211.5% between 1990-2012 while agricultural land fell 18.86%

title: Land developers sell plots based on unverified boundaries and documents
description: In the absence of strong regulatory oversight, land developers in fast-growing urban and peri-urban areas have sold housing plots without properly verifying boundaries or map accuracy, leading buyers into disputes over land they believed they had legitimately purchased.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Rental housing market lacks standard tenant protections
description: Nepal's rental housing sector operates with an imbalanced landlord-tenant relationship, where landlords can set largely arbitrary rents and terms, and there is little standardized contract framework or dispute-resolution mechanism to protect tenants, particularly migrant renters in Kathmandu.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Fragmented jurisdiction between federal, provincial, and local land authorities
description: Overlapping and unclear authority between federal, provincial, and local governments over land administration and urban planning has repeatedly stalled reform implementation, with land agencies frequently blaming each other for lack of progress on record modernization and dispute resolution.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Weak building-code enforcement outside high-profile reconstruction zones
description: Although Nepal updated its national building code and seismic standards after the 2015 earthquake, local governments say they lack the technical expertise and resources to enforce these codes for everyday private construction, meaning much new building may not meet updated safety standards.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: No standardized property valuation or title-insurance system
description: Nepal lacks a widely used, standardized property valuation methodology or title insurance product, making it harder for buyers, lenders, and courts to establish fair market value or protect against undiscovered title defects when property changes hands.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Diaspora Nepalis struggle to manage or invest in property remotely
description: Nepalis working abroad who want to invest remittance savings into land or housing back home often face difficulty verifying property details, managing transactions, or overseeing construction remotely, given the lack of digitized, trustworthy end-to-end property services.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Agricultural land steadily lost to unplanned urban conversion
description: Fertile agricultural land ringing Kathmandu Valley and other urban centers is increasingly converted into housing plots without formal land-use planning, reducing domestic food-production capacity even as urban housing itself remains poorly regulated.
severity_or_scale: Agricultural land in Kathmandu Valley fell 18.86% from 1990-2012 while built-up area rose 211.5%

title: Millions of Nepalis work abroad, concentrated in a few risky destinations
description: Over 3.5 million Nepali citizens work abroad, with the vast majority concentrated in Gulf Cooperation Council countries and Malaysia, destinations known for demanding manual labor conditions, limited legal protections under sponsorship-based employment systems, and high migrant mortality.
severity_or_scale: 3.5 million+ Nepalis working abroad; 500,000+ in Malaysia, ~1.3 million in GCC states; 88% concentrated in GCC/Malaysia

title: Migrant worker deaths abroad remain persistently high
description: Close to 4,700 Nepali migrant workers died abroad between 2019 and 2023, with an average of three bodies returning to Nepal every day, a toll made more troubling because most were certified medically fit before departure, raising questions about workplace conditions and reporting.
severity_or_scale: ~4,700 deaths 2019-2023; ~3 bodies returned daily; suicide accounts for ~11% of deaths over the past decade

title: Recruitment agency and broker fraud traps migrants in debt
description: Fraudulent recruitment schemes involving fake job offers, forged visas, and inflated fees have swindled hundreds of aspiring migrant workers, with most complaints filed against unlicensed individual agents rather than the registered manpower companies that structurally evade accountability.
severity_or_scale: Over 500 formal fraud complaints filed in a 10-month period 2024-2025; claimed property damage over Rs 1 billion in the same period

title: Widespread abuse and exploitation of migrant workers abroad
description: More than a third of surveyed migrant workers report facing verbal, emotional, or physical abuse at their overseas workplace, with deceptive recruitment about job terms sometimes escalating into forced labor or debt bondage once workers arrive and cannot easily leave.
severity_or_scale: Over one-third of migrant workers report facing abuse

title: High recruitment fees push migrants into debt before they even start working
description: Despite regulations meant to shift recruitment costs to employers, many Nepali migrants still pay substantial fees to agents to secure jobs abroad, often borrowing at high interest to cover these costs, debt they must repay from wages earned under difficult conditions.
severity_or_scale: 88% of surveyed Nepali workers in Malaysia in one study paid recruitment fees

title: Bans on young women's migration for domestic work drive unsafe irregular routes
description: Repeated government restrictions on women migrating to the Gulf for domestic work, intended to prevent abuse, have instead pushed many women to migrate through informal or illegal channels with unlicensed brokers, increasing their vulnerability to trafficking and exploitation.
severity_or_scale: An estimated 60,000-100,000 Nepali women work as Gulf domestic workers, mostly through informal channels

title: Returnee migrant workers struggle to find jobs back home
description: A large share of returning migrant workers remain unemployed long after coming home, and most who do find work cannot use the skills they gained abroad, since domestic industries rarely match the trades workers practiced overseas, wasting years of accumulated experience.
severity_or_scale: 24% of male and 60% of female returnees unemployed 6+ months after return; only 22% use skills acquired abroad domestically

title: Irregular migrants are excluded from government reintegration support
description: Nepal's formal reintegration programs, including soft loans and skills-matching support for returnees, explicitly exclude workers who migrated through irregular or undocumented channels, leaving the most vulnerable returnees without institutional support at home.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: High youth unemployment continues to drive the migration cycle
description: With domestic job creation failing to keep pace with the number of young people entering the workforce each year, foreign labor migration functions as a de facto national employment policy, perpetuating a cycle where reintegration programs cannot succeed without parallel growth in domestic opportunity.
severity_or_scale: Youth unemployment rate of 20.8% in 2024

title: Skills mismatch between graduates and employer needs persists
description: Employers across sectors report difficulty finding workers with practical, job-ready skills, while graduates report difficulty finding jobs matching their qualifications, a disconnect rooted in outdated academic and vocational curricula that have not kept pace with labor market demand.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Low female labor force participation limits household and national income
description: Nepal's female labor force participation rate is roughly half that of men, driven substantially by social expectations that women shoulder domestic responsibilities, restricting the economic contribution and financial independence of a huge share of the working-age population.
severity_or_scale: Female labor force participation ~22.7-28.7% versus much higher male participation

title: Unpaid care work is a major structural barrier to women's paid employment
description: The large majority of Nepali women perform substantial unpaid domestic and care work, nearly six hours daily on average, with mothers of young children showing especially low paid-work participation, reflecting a near-total absence of affordable childcare options.
severity_or_scale: 86% of Nepali women engage in unpaid care work; women spend 5.9 hrs/day on domestic work vs 2.25 hrs for men

title: Human trafficking exploits economic desperation, especially of women and girls
description: Tens of Nepali women and girls are trafficked into India daily, often by relatives or acquaintances, for forced labor, forced marriage, or sexual exploitation, with poverty, lack of local opportunity, and a porous open border creating a persistent trafficking corridor.
severity_or_scale: At least 54 girls/women trafficked into India daily; 12,000-15,000 girls aged 6-16 trafficked annually

title: Elderly parents left behind as working-age children migrate
description: With a large share of households having at least one member who migrated abroad in the past decade, many elderly parents, especially women, are left without a co-resident caregiver, taking on increased physical, economic, and emotional burdens with limited institutional elder-care support.
severity_or_scale: 47% of Nepali households had at least one member migrate in the previous 10 years

title: Cross-sector brain drain extends well beyond medicine
description: Skilled professionals across engineering, IT, academia, and business increasingly migrate for better pay and opportunity abroad, following the same pattern seen in medicine, depleting the pool of experienced talent available to grow Nepal's private sector and public institutions.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Bribery and informal payments remain routine for basic public services
description: Citizens seeking routine government services such as utility connections, licenses, and permits frequently report being asked for unofficial facilitation payments to get their paperwork processed, with unnecessary document demands and procedural hassle used as leverage to extract bribes.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified precisely (widely reported pattern across multiple surveys)

title: Passport, license, and document issuance suffers chronic delays
description: Offices responsible for issuing passports and driving licenses are notorious for slow processing, with citizens frequently reporting long queues, repeated office visits, and unpredictable timelines for services that should be routine and fast.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified
source: general knowledge / Kathmandu Post governance coverage

title: Local governments lack capacity to implement digital services
description: Since federalism devolved many service-delivery responsibilities to local governments, many municipalities and rural municipalities lack trained IT staff and technical infrastructure to run e-governance systems effectively, undermining national digitization initiatives at the point citizens actually interact with government.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Digital ID system rollout hampered by continued demand for paper documents
description: Despite building a national digital identity app (Nagarik) intended to reduce paperwork, many government offices continue to insist on physical documents anyway, undermining the efficiency gains the digital system was meant to deliver and confusing citizens about which channel to use.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Judiciary case backlog denies timely justice to citizens
description: Nepal's courts, including the Supreme Court, have accumulated tens of thousands of pending cases, some unresolved for over a decade due to insufficient judges, weak case-flow management systems, and rising case complexity, with some litigants reportedly dying before their case concludes.
severity_or_scale: Supreme Court had 27,000-28,000+ pending cases; over 4,000 pending more than 5 years; some cases pending nearly 20 years

title: Weak cooperative-sector oversight enabled a massive embezzlement scandal
description: Nepal's roughly 30,000 savings and credit cooperatives are only loosely regulated, with the Department of Cooperatives lacking the staff and enforcement authority for proper supervision, a gap that allowed operators to embezzle depositor savings on a national scale before regulators intervened.
severity_or_scale: 30,000+ cooperatives nationally; at least Rs 87.89 billion embezzled

title: Government ministries operate in data and systems silos
description: Different government departments run duplicative, non-interoperable digital systems, a problem identified in analyses over a decade ago that persists today, forcing citizens to resubmit the same information repeatedly to different agencies and blocking efficient service delivery.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Entrenched bureaucracy resists reform and ministerial direction
description: Nepal's civil service is described as having grown sufficiently powerful, backed by political patronage networks, to slow, reshape, or quietly resist reform initiatives from ministers or the prime minister, meaning policy announcements often fail to translate into changed practice on the ground.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Weak local enforcement of building and safety codes
description: National building codes strengthened after the 2015 earthquake are inconsistently enforced at the local level, with municipalities reporting they lack the trained engineers and resources needed to inspect and approve construction against updated seismic standards.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Frequent policy reversals create uncertainty for citizens and businesses
description: Rules around issues like student No Objection Certificates, women's migration for domestic work, and remittance regulations have been repeatedly introduced, tightened, loosened, and reversed by successive governments, making it hard for citizens and businesses to plan around a stable policy environment.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified
source: general knowledge (pattern documented across NOC and migration policy reporting)

title: Overlapping federal-provincial-local jurisdiction delays infrastructure delivery
description: Nepal's 2015 shift to federalism created three tiers of government with often unclear or overlapping authority over infrastructure and land, and jurisdictional disputes between these levels have repeatedly stalled projects like the Melamchi water scheme and land-record reform.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified
source: general knowledge / Melamchi and land reform coverage

title: Public procurement delays stall infrastructure projects for years
description: Major public infrastructure projects in Nepal, from water supply to hydropower to roads, are frequently delayed for years past original timelines due to contractor disputes, financing gaps, and slow government decision-making, as seen vividly in the multi-decade Melamchi water project saga.
severity_or_scale: Melamchi project began in 1998 and remained incomplete over 25 years later per recent reporting

title: Corruption perceived as directly linked to poor institutional service delivery
description: A recent citizen survey found that Nepalis directly link corruption to delays and poor performance in public institutions, suggesting that anti-corruption reform and service-delivery reform are seen by the public as inseparable problems rather than separate issues.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Earthquake preparedness has advanced little since 2015
description: Despite the trauma of the 2015 earthquakes that killed around 9,000 people and destroyed over half a million structures, reporting a decade later found little concrete improvement in disaster preparedness, including search-and-rescue capacity and retrofit of vulnerable older buildings.
severity_or_scale: 2015 earthquakes killed ~9,000 and damaged/destroyed 500,000+ structures

title: Building codes strengthened on paper but poorly enforced in practice
description: New, stricter seismic building codes adopted after 2015 have not translated into consistently safer construction nationwide, since local governments say they lack the trained engineers and resources to inspect and enforce compliance for the large volume of private construction happening across the country.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Glacial lake outburst floods and flash floods are intensifying with climate change
description: Rapid warming in Nepal's high mountains, nearly twice the global average rate since 1940, is destabilizing glaciers and permafrost, increasing the risk of catastrophic glacial lake outburst floods and landslide-triggered flash floods that can devastate entire valleys with little warning.
severity_or_scale: A 2026 glacier-collapse flood event killed 1,300+ people, left 5,300+ missing, and affected an estimated 90,000 people; local warming of 4.7°F since 1940

title: Monsoon landslides are a recurring, deadly annual hazard
description: Nepal's steep terrain, intensifying monsoon rainfall, and poorly engineered new roads combine to produce landslides that kill people, destroy homes, and cut off communities nearly every rainy season, a pattern repeated for decades including major events in 2012, 2015, and 2017.
severity_or_scale: The 2015 earthquake alone triggered over 20,000 landslides across 14 districts

title: Kathmandu's air pollution is among the worst in the world
description: Vehicle emissions, which alone contribute roughly 38% of particulate pollution, combined with road dust, construction, and brick kilns have pushed Kathmandu's air quality to hazardous levels, especially in winter, driving up rates of respiratory disease and other pollution-linked illness.
severity_or_scale: PM2.5 levels reported at 384 µg/m³ in 2025, over 25x the WHO safe limit of 15 µg/m³; registered vehicles grew 32x from 2000 to 2016

title: Solid waste management crisis chokes Kathmandu Valley
description: The roughly 3.3 million residents of Kathmandu Valley's municipalities generate over 1,200 tonnes of solid waste daily, most of which is landfilled, openly dumped, or burned, with the search for viable, socially-accepted landfill sites remaining a source of chronic local conflict.
severity_or_scale: 1,200+ tonnes of municipal solid waste generated daily in Kathmandu Valley

title: Plastic pollution is destroying Kathmandu's rivers
description: Roughly 70,000 plastic fragments travel down the Bagmati River through Kathmandu Valley every day, part of a broader pattern where a large share of the valley's solid waste ends up dumped directly into rivers, rendering long stretches of the once-sacred Bagmati unfit for aquatic life, irrigation, or drinking.
severity_or_scale: ~70,000 plastic fragments/day in the Bagmati River; Nepal generates 450+ tonnes of plastic waste daily nationwide

title: Kathmandu Valley's groundwater is being depleted faster than it recharges
description: Overpumping of groundwater combined with paved-over recharge areas has caused the valley's water table to drop by as much as one to several meters per year in places, drying up traditional wells and stone spouts that many residents, especially the poor, still depend on for water.
severity_or_scale: Groundwater level declining ~1 meter/year on average, up to 2.5 meters/year in some areas; ~30% of Kathmandu's wells reported drying up

title: Mount Everest and high-mountain trekking regions face a growing waste crisis
description: Surging numbers of climbers and trekkers combined with the near-total absence of waste management or sanitation facilities on the mountain has left an estimated 200 tons of trash accumulating annually on Everest, much of which does not decompose in the cold, permanently high-altitude environment.
severity_or_scale: ~200 tons of trash left on Everest annually

title: Weak early-warning systems leave communities exposed to flash floods
description: Despite the known and growing risk of glacial lake outburst floods and flash floods in high-mountain river valleys, community-level early warning infrastructure and evacuation planning remain limited in many at-risk districts, contributing to high casualty tolls when disasters strike.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified precisely, evidenced by high casualty/missing tolls in the 2026 flood event

title: Climate change is reducing crop yields through drought and new pest pressure
description: Warmer winters have brought more frequent armyworm attacks on maize and greater prevalence of rice blast disease, compounding the direct yield losses from delayed monsoons and winter droughts that smallholder farmers with limited irrigation access are least equipped to absorb.
severity_or_scale: Delayed monsoon/drought linked to up to 20% rice yield reduction in some Terai districts

title: Deforestation for firewood and construction accelerates soil erosion
description: Continued reliance on firewood for cooking, especially in mountain districts, and demand for construction timber contribute to deforestation on steep slopes, which in turn increases soil erosion and landslide susceptibility, compounding Nepal's broader disaster vulnerability.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Haphazard urbanization has increased Kathmandu Valley's disaster exposure
description: Unplanned construction that ignores hazard-zone mapping, combined with the loss of open, water-absorbing land to concrete, has made Kathmandu Valley significantly more vulnerable to both earthquake damage and urban flash flooding than a more carefully planned city would be.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Waste management lacks a coherent decision-support and planning system
description: Kathmandu Valley municipalities have struggled for over a decade to develop a coordinated, data-driven solid waste management plan, resulting in ad hoc responses like emergency landfill searches rather than systematic investment in recycling, composting, or waste-to-energy infrastructure.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Cash-on-delivery dominance reflects low trust in digital transactions
description: Most Nepali online shoppers, especially first-time buyers, still prefer to pay cash upon delivery rather than online, reflecting limited confidence in digital payment security and a preference to verify goods physically before paying, which raises operating costs and cash-handling risk for sellers.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified precisely (described as majority preference among Nepali online shoppers)

title: High rates of delivery failure and order errors undermine e-commerce
description: A meaningful share of online orders in Nepal never arrive, arrive as the wrong item, or arrive damaged, reflecting underdeveloped logistics infrastructure, heavy reliance on third-party couriers, and limited warehousing outside major cities.
severity_or_scale: 8.7% of orders reportedly never arrive; 9.7% arrive as wrong items; 8.0% arrive damaged

title: Weak return and refund processes discourage repeat online shopping
description: Returning unsatisfactory goods is difficult in much of Nepal's e-commerce market due to logistics constraints and inconsistent seller policies, and the resulting lack of consumer trust around returns, product authenticity, and payment security discourages customers from shopping online again.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: E-commerce logistics infrastructure concentrated in a few hub cities
description: Warehousing for online retail is concentrated near Kathmandu, Birgunj, and Pokhara, meaning customers and small sellers outside these hubs face longer delivery times, higher shipping costs, and less product availability than the more built-out urban market.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Informal retailers lack basic digital point-of-sale and inventory tools
description: The vast majority of small shops and traders in Nepal still track sales and inventory manually, with little adoption of even basic digital point-of-sale systems, making it hard to manage stock, detect losses, or access the sales data formal lenders or investors would want to see.
severity_or_scale: SMEs make up over 90% of business establishments in Nepal

title: Limited secure payment gateway access for small online merchants
description: Small Nepali online sellers face hurdles integrating secure, affordable digital payment gateways into their storefronts, pushing much of the market toward cash-on-delivery or informal payment collection methods rather than streamlined checkout experiences common in more developed e-commerce markets.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Unreliable rural internet limits e-commerce market expansion
description: E-commerce growth outside Kathmandu is constrained by inconsistent internet connectivity and low smartphone penetration in many districts, meaning online retailers' addressable market remains concentrated in urban areas even as national internet statistics show broader nominal coverage.
severity_or_scale: 47% of population online via broadband nationally, with urban-rural gaps

title: Counterfeit and substandard goods circulate through informal and online retail
description: Weak market surveillance and product-quality enforcement allow counterfeit or substandard goods, from electronics to food products, to be sold through informal retail channels and increasingly through online marketplaces, with consumers having little recourse once a purchase is made.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Retail digitization gap between Kathmandu and the rest of the country
description: Digital retail tools, delivery apps, and online marketplaces have grown quickly in Kathmandu Valley but remain far less available or used in Nepal's smaller cities and rural market towns, meaning the benefits of e-commerce growth are unevenly distributed geographically.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Melamchi water project delays have kept Kathmandu chronically under-supplied
description: The Melamchi Water Supply Project, meant to solve Kathmandu Valley's decades-long drinking water shortage by tunneling river water from a neighboring district, has suffered repeated delays from contractor disputes, corruption allegations, and monsoon flood damage since construction began in 1998, leaving residents still reliant on inconsistent alternative sources.
severity_or_scale: Project launched in 1998, still not fully complete after 25+ years; delivers up to 170 million liters/day when operational

title: Only a small share of Nepalis have access to safely managed drinking water
description: While the large majority of Nepalis have access to a basic drinking water source, only a small share of the population enjoys water meeting the higher safely-managed standard, free from contamination and reliably available on premises, leaving most households exposed to water-quality risk.
severity_or_scale: 88% have basic drinking water access, but only 27% have safely managed drinking water

title: Fecal contamination common even in officially improved water sources
description: Testing has found that a large majority of household drinking water drawn from officially designated improved sources still tests positive for fecal contamination, meaning formal water-source classification does not reliably indicate the water is actually safe to drink.
severity_or_scale: 81.2% of improved-source household water tested positive for fecal contamination in a 2014 study

title: Open defecation persists despite Nepal's official open-defecation-free status
description: Nepal declared itself open-defecation-free in 2019, but a meaningful share of the population, particularly in remote and poor rural areas, continues to practice open defecation due to lack of functional latrines, water access, or sustained behavior-change support.
severity_or_scale: 16% of the population still practices open defecation despite the 2019 declaration

title: Poorest rural households have far worse water access than the wealthy
description: Piped water connections directly into the home or yard are concentrated among wealthier households, while poorer rural families more often rely on shared public water points, meaning the burden of water collection time and quality risk falls disproportionately on those least able to bear it.
severity_or_scale: 35% of richest households have in-home/courtyard piped water access, compared to far less for poorer quintiles

title: Millions lack access to even basic sanitation infrastructure
description: Despite national progress narratives, several million Nepalis still lack access to improved sanitation facilities and basic water services altogether, concentrated in remote hill and Terai communities that formal WASH programs have not yet reached.
severity_or_scale: 10.8 million people lack access to improved sanitation; 3.5 million lack basic water services

title: Water resource management is fragmented across multiple agencies
description: Responsibility for drinking water, irrigation, groundwater regulation, and river management in Nepal is split across multiple federal, provincial, and local bodies without a single coordinating authority, contributing to problems like unchecked groundwater overextraction and unresolved multi-decade project delays like Melamchi.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified
source: general knowledge / Melamchi and WASH governance coverage

title: Water user committees often lack capacity to maintain rural schemes
description: Many rural drinking-water and irrigation schemes are handed over to local water user committees after construction, but these volunteer bodies frequently lack the technical training or funding to maintain pumps and pipes, causing schemes to fall into disrepair within a few years.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Kathmandu's groundwater over-extraction threatens long-term water security
description: With surface-water infrastructure like Melamchi delayed for decades, Kathmandu Valley residents and institutions increasingly rely on groundwater pumped faster than it can naturally recharge, threatening the long-term viability of the very backup source people depend on during shortages.
severity_or_scale: Groundwater level declining ~1 meter/year on average, up to 2.5m/year in some areas

title: Latrine coverage does not guarantee actual latrine use
description: National statistics on latrine coverage can overstate real sanitation improvements, since studies in rural villages have found meaningful gaps between having a latrine built and household members consistently using it, due to habit, water availability, or maintenance issues.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified precisely (documented gap in a rural Eastern Nepal case study)

title: Informal, cash-based operation excludes most SMEs from the formal economy
description: A large share of Nepal's small businesses are too small, too cash-based, or too averse to regulatory compliance costs to formally register, which locks them out of formal credit, government support programs, and the tax base, a lose-lose for both business owners and government revenue.
severity_or_scale: SMEs represent 90%+ of business establishments but contribute only ~25% of GDP

title: Dual bookkeeping practices reflect weak accounting infrastructure
description: Many Nepali SMEs reportedly maintain two sets of books, one for tax purposes and one reflecting actual performance, a practice enabled by weak accounting capacity among both business owners and tax officials, undermining accurate financial data that could otherwise support better business decisions or access to credit.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified

title: Low digital literacy blocks adoption of even basic business software
description: Widespread gaps in digital skills, especially among older business owners and those in rural areas, mean many SMEs cannot effectively use accounting, inventory, or point-of-sale software even where it is available and affordable, limiting productivity gains from digitization efforts.
severity_or_scale: National digital literacy estimated at only ~31%

title: Startup funding schemes announced by government have gone largely undisbursed
description: Nepal's government has periodically announced startup support programs, including a 2015-16 challenge fund and a 2019-20 cash subsidy scheme, that produced little to no actual funding disbursement before being quietly discontinued, leaving entrepreneurs unable to rely on promised public support.
severity_or_scale: A 2015-16 startup challenge fund produced zero disbursements

title: High collateral requirements block SME access to growth capital
description: Banks typically require collateral valued well above the loan amount, a barrier that disproportionately affects newer or smaller businesses without significant fixed assets, forcing many SMEs to rely on personal savings or informal lenders instead of scaling with formal credit.
severity_or_scale: Collateral requirements averaging ~130% of loan value
source: general knowledge / Nepal MSME finance research

title: Complex procedures deter foreign investment into Nepali startups
description: International investors and Nepali founders alike describe bringing foreign venture capital into a Nepali company as complex and slow, involving multiple regulatory approvals that discourage the kind of early-stage foreign investment common in more startup-friendly markets.
severity_or_scale: impact not quantified
